items.title: Blackstone stake buy to boost IIFL Finance's capital needs: Fitch Ratings
items.rss_summary: Blackstone's plan to acquire a 16 per cent stake in IIFL Finance will support the Indian firm's growth capital with an unlikely shift in IIFL's business model, which focuses on secured loans, Fitch Ratings said on Thursday. Fitch said with the investment, Blackstone would effectively become IIFL Finance's main private-equity shareholder. Fitch believes that the refreshed shareholder and board composition could alter IIFL's business strategy, risk appetite and growth trajectory. However, the significant injection of capital and foreign investment supports Indian financial institutions' capital and funding flexibility. Earlier this month, the board of IIFL Finance approved a plan to raise Rs 6,414 crore through a preferential issue. This included Rs 5,000 crore investment from Blackstone and Rs 1,264 crore by the company's promoters Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman, besides Rs 150 crore from Anchorage Capital. items.title: TCI Express to invest ₹500 crore in 5 years to expand logistics infra
items.rss_summary: Logistics solutions company TCI Express Ltd on Thursday announced a Rs 500-crore infrastructure expansion plan for the next five years and the opening of three sorting centres in Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Kolkata, strengthening its nationwide express delivery network. Through these strategic investments, the company said it aims to build a future-ready logistics ecosystem, enhance service capabilities and reinforce its position as one of India's leading players in the sector. The company said it has already invested Rs 500 crore in the last seven years, and now intends to direct the new investment to high-performing verticals. "We are witnessing strong growth momentum across our business verticals, particularly domestic air express and e-commerce express, which have emerged as key growth drivers in FY2027. Our next phase of expansion will focus on strengthening the capabilities of individual verticals, enhancing operational efficiencies and building a more agile and scalable network,"

items.title: Rupee slides 8 paise to 93.49 against US dollar during early trade
items.rss_summary: The rupee slipped 8 paise to 93.49 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, weighed down by a strong greenback and weak domestic equity markets. However, lower crude oil prices and foreign-fund inflows capped the rupee's fall, forex traders said. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.40 and declined to 93.49 against the greenback, registering a loss of 8 paise from its previous close. The domestic currency climbed 10 paise to close at 93.41 against US dollar on Wednesday after gaining 68 paise in the preceding two sessions. "The decline in crude prices and RBI's actions to curb speculative activity in the currency have helped the rupee gain strength. In the near-term, the rupee is likely to trade in the 93.20 to 94 range," said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments.
